text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an i5 eDrive35L states the air suspension, which the fuel 5 Series lacks, makes the ride more comfortable. Owner states a full charge gave only about 330 km at -2 C in winter. Owner objects that streaming apps and the heated steering wheel require paid unlocks. Owner states lane-centring assist requires hands on the wheel, comparing it unfavourably with a Toyota Camry. Owner states the parking radar sensors often give false alerts in winter.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an i5 eDrive40L states real-world range is close to the official figure and the battery drains slowly when parked. Owner states the door panels and centre console feel like hard plastic and the 2025 update removed the silver trim. Owner states the EV is packaged like a fuel car with a raised rear floor. Owner states the single rear motor makes the front feel light and passengers may get carsick.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an i5 eDrive40L (previously a 3 Series owner) states ride comfort is the best of any generation. Owner states the rear middle seat is uncomfortable with three passengers. Owner rates value as very high, getting a mid-spec 5 Series for the price of an older 3 Series.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an i5 eDrive35L states the blue upholstery, wood trim, crystal details and ambient lighting make the cabin feel luxurious. Owner states the Harman Kardon system no longer allows user EQ or surround adjustment, worse than in their previous 325i. Owner states energy use is 13-14 kWh/100 km in May and range in B mode exceeds 600 km.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an i5 eDrive35L states the crystal ambient lighting and wireless CarPlay were key reasons for buying. Owner states the EV drives like a fuel car but responds more quickly. Owner states the voice assistant triggers too easily compared with their old 3 Series. Owner states the driver assistance suits people who prefer traditional driving rather than end-to-end smart driving systems.
